source_locations.location: Crystal Structure of LiCe(BH4)3Cl; Figures 2 and 3

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The cubic structure (I-43m) contains isolated [Ce4Cl4(BH4)12]4− clusters with distorted-cubane Ce4Cl4 cores, charge-balanced by disordered Li+ ions occupying two-thirds of the 12d sites. Each Ce coordinates three chloride ions and three borohydride groups. The deuterated sample used for neutron diffraction was analyzed as an isotopic version of this phase.

synthesis.procedure: CeCl3 and LiBH4 mixtures in molar ratios of 1:2, 1:3, or 1:4 were ball-milled under argon. Milling comprised 60 repetitions of 2 min milling followed by 2 min pauses, with main-disk and planetary-disk speeds of 200 and 560 rpm, respectively. Preparation and handling took place in an argon glovebox.
synthesis.time: 60 repetitions of 2 min milling and 2 min pause
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Fritsch Pulverisette 4 planetary mill; 80 mL tungsten-carbide containers and tungsten-carbide balls; approximate sample-to-balls mass ratio 1:35

title: LiCe(BH4)3Cl, a New Lithium-Ion Conductor and Hydrogen Storage Material with Isolated Tetranuclear Anionic Clusters
